claim: Adjacency and substitution support the proposed universal personal-pronoun analysis.
evidence_summary: To us both behaves as one constituent. Compare outside of us two and you two.
finding: Evidence for one NP leaves wordhood open. First-, second- and third-person forms need separate controls.
inference: Do adjacency and substitution identify a word, or only an NP constituent?

evidence.passage: §10.1, p. 427. Adjacency and substitution support the proposed universal personal-pronoun analysis.
evidence.example: In to us both the two words can form a single complement of to. The personal forms also combine with two in independently documented phrases (pp. 639, 1466). More than one word can occupy that same constituent position.
evidence.establishes: Constituency follows more readily than single-word status. The distributions of us, you and them require separate controls.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
